correctness.rationale: Exact subset support combinatorics give the finite width formula. Gaussian orthogonal projection and chi-square concentration yield spherical equivalence. Gaussian order-statistic Poisson convergence plus an explicit uniform geometric-tail bound prove the infinite-series limit. Suppressed class terms vanish as the smaller part tends to infinity. The deterministic 2^(1-p)b_n² shift yields the critical log-log crossover. Gamma-log identities determine moments; a one-sided exponential tail proves non-Gaussianity. The included checker tests 520 exhaustive finite supports and 60,000 independent samples but does not substitute for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A genuinely geometric, natural family of graph associahedra has an exact non-Gaussian width law and a sharp logarithmic-in-logarithm bipartition transition. The shift cannot be inferred from a generic Gaussian maximum: it depends on enumerating connected subsets and tracking a shrinking but divergent color class. Complete fluctuation law, mean, variance and the threshold classify an asymptotic regime of interest in random support optimization.
